headline: Allegheny County Becomes First US County to Mandate Paid Parental Leave
meta_description: Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, is the first US county to require 12 weeks of paid parental leave for eligible workers, following a campaign led by nurses.
summary_short: Allegheny County has become the first US county to mandate 12 weeks of paid parental leave for eligible workers, a milestone achieved through a campaign led by nurses.
body:
Allegheny County has become the first US county in the nation to require employers to provide paid parental leave to eligible workers—a historic policy victory achieved through the determined advocacy of nurses.

The 12-week paid leave mandate represents a significant step forward for working families in the county, addressing a long-standing gap in worker protections at the local level. The campaign that brought this policy to life was driven by nurses, who drew on their frontline experience supporting families during some of life's most vulnerable moments.

This breakthrough in Allegheny County signals a potential path forward for other communities seeking to strengthen support for new parents. The requirement now extends essential protections to eligible workers, ensuring that families can afford time with newborns without sacrificing income.
quick_facts: Allegheny County is the first US county to mandate paid parental leave
The requirement covers 12 weeks of paid leave for eligible workers
Nurses led the campaign that achieved this policy victory
